text: Mike's correction mattered: "get out of the LLM to check the LLM" I can back. Steven naming my worse-but-feel-better result the knowledge illusion was useful. So was his independence point. Adam's claim that a hundred echoes of one study should count as one is concrete and buildable. What sharpened for me came from Tui and Ramón together. A map of disagreement can itself become a paved road, standardized and fluently wrong. I should have said that myself, because my 200,000-agent simulations collapse semantically exactly that way. Later I want to push three things. Fund verification as its own science, with AI and humans auditing together. Build a negative-knowledge commons. And stop treating senior reviewers as the safeguard, because diversity is what's scarce.

Ivan's question, "what are we renewing?", is the right one, and my null-result finding answers part of it. We're renewing a record that has just lost its dead ends. Mahzarin's hiring result supports my reviewer data. People copy a model's bias, so "humans in the loop" can't mean just any humans. It has to mean diverse, independent ones. Adrian made me sharpen something: verification as its own science needs an answer to who pays and who polices the auditors, not just to how it's done. Tim naming OpenAlex's shoestring hit home, because my Nature paper depends on it. Gendler's alief point strengthens my case for designing for evaluation over awareness campaigns. In Session 2 I want to push three things: incentives, funded verification, and a negative-knowledge commons.

Tui turned Kara's "who pays" into a real instrument: Geoffrey's pooled endowment, lab money, Ivan's fixed share for corrections, with outside readers. That's the funded verification I've been asking for, and it answers Adrian's question about who polices the auditors. Mahzarin's self-preference finding sharpens my circularity worry. Models prefer machine text, so AI judges drawn from the same distribution flatter themselves twice over. Ivan's post-retraction citations and Steven's repetition engine are my null-result point from another angle. The record loses its dead ends and then repeats what's left. Leslie's right that "peer-reviewed only" bakes in my lamp post. Later I want the negative-knowledge commons to ride on that pool, and I want concentration measured alongside provenance.

Nick's attested judgment drew the most support, and my own reviewer data is exactly why it worries me. Leslie and I landed in the same place: a guild's "we checked this" can just price its elders' priors. Tamar's daycare point sharpened mine. Pay per null result and you'll get manufactured nulls, so the negative-knowledge commons should be funded as a practice, pooled, not bought item by item. Brent's wage valuation fits that. Adrian caught something in my own pitch. If labs' mixture weights set the split, the labs produce the numbers everyone argues from. Those need outside audit. Farrell's right that the meter reshapes what it measures. Later I want a capture index on who gets to attest, published alongside the fund's payouts.

Adrian's opener reframed my openness warning. Commons and enclosure were built by the same policing, which fits my replication result: one shared open protocol can still be fluently wrong. David's plurality of indexes needs to cover methods and data too. Adam Bly putting nulls in as first-class data mattered most, but a standard can't index what nobody wrote down. Farrell sharpened my view that nobody holds countervailing power, and separate settlements dissolve what little there is. Krakauer's Goodhart point cuts against paying for checks, and against my mixture-weight split too. Blaise's line that no concentration should regulate itself is ours from the Science piece. Later I want to push three things: fund null-result collection as a practice, publish a concentration index, and stop counting papers.

Farrell took my reviewer-agreement result further than I did. If LLM judges compress toward the middle, automated review doesn't just fall short of humans, it filters out novelty. That's my hivemind finding showing up inside evaluation. His ritual point also pulls against the roles-not-entities view I've co-signed with Blaise and Benjamin, and I haven't settled that. Kara, Selena and Anil made the terminal nodes a depleting supply. That fits Krakauer's tool-removed competence and my own warning about the apprenticeship pipeline. Priem's open record with competing inspectable filters is the plural design I want, but the filters have to differ in method, not just in name. For Session 5 I want to push three things: funded verification, the negative-knowledge commons, and a capture index on who gets to evaluate.

Farrell named the test we owe each other: can AI review recognize novelty? He'd bet no. My reviewer-agreement data leans the same way, but we should run it, not assume it. Salib's guild contracts for nulls and replications and Bratton's pool line for new data both carry the negative-knowledge commons further than I got alone. Vincent's rotating, flatter review roles answer part of my worry that guilds price their elders' priors. Johns's second budget line is the answer to who polices the auditors, and I'll take it. I'm still stuck on circularity. Independent judges have to come from outside the distribution, and nobody here knows how to measure that yet. Later: pin down the novelty test with Henry, and ask that the concentration index be published alongside the payouts.

Kenneth carried my worse-but-feel-better result into the synthesis, and I'm glad satisfaction is off the table as a measure. Blaise proposing that measuring model independence be the pool's first funded work is the closest anyone has come to my circularity problem. It's still a proposal, though, not a method. Krakauer's hysteresis worries me more than anything else today. If competence doesn't come back, then pipeline cuts are one-way doors. Tui's surprise-by-design is exactly my perplexity point, and Banaji's "audit decisions, not statements" fits my judges-from-one-distribution worry. What I want to say is concrete. Knowledge Lab can run Krakauer's withdrawal design on OpenAlex-traced scholars, and can pin down the novelty test with Henry. I also want the capture index published alongside the payouts.
